decision: Accept the bounded synthetic diagnostic as evidence for the typed integration: all 24 seven-slot original/native accounts match exactly; all 24 two-slot controls reproduce native withholding of SOL while the original account admits it after same-cycle exits. All 96 artifacts reproduce exactly from frozen source and 5328 independent Decimal checks reconcile. This is process-local research instrumentation, not a deployed implementation or historical profitability result. Implement the typed source/calendar entry-routing adapter next, retaining full native actions and withholding, atomic account ownership and original source intent anchors; reconcile configured native exits and full holding clocks before allowing those closes to drive the account.
falsifier: Changed source/configuration/anchor identity, native/current position boundary mismatch, unexplained seven-slot account difference, lost two-slot counterexample, incorrect raw action/withholding fields, nonmatching archive artifact or failed independent quantity/fee/funding/cash reconciliation invalidates the corresponding diagnostic. One-hour synthetic results do not establish terminal source coverage, HYPE soft/hard or UNKNOWN compatibility, full native transport, actual historical profitability or live defects.
hypothesis: Applying native entry admissions at the true decision-position boundary can preserve native capacity and configured-exit withholding while retaining source-priced account economics.
limitations: All decisions and source prices are explicitly programmed synthetic 2030 fixtures; no prospective or actual historical account outcome was evaluated.
Seven and two slots are distinct declared diagnostic controls; only seven matches the current configuration. No live capacity change was made.
The prototype patches the research entry function only inside its own process. A typed production research integration remains to be implemented and qualified.
Native configured closes are retained as observations. Original frozen account exits still execute; a matched synthetic ETH recipe timestamp does not qualify all native exit behavior.
Only one hour of a two-day replay contract is supplied. All observed positions close, but terminal evaluator acceptance is not claimed.
HYPE soft/hard holds, future UNKNOWN behavior, full native transport, historical source-age receipts and complete historical financial effects remain unqualified.
The initial probe supplied resolved static targets as dynamic anchors and failed before writing a case; corrected binding uses original source intent anchors and validates resolved barriers.
